params.body:
## Why

On the French site the flow picker, the flow page heading and the header subtitle showed the general flow under its Dutch name, "Algemeen". Flow names had one language only; their taglines were already translated.

## What changes

- **Flows can carry their name per language.** `labels` on a flow and `subtitles` on its brand, keyed by language code, next to the existing `taglines`. Without them the single `label` and `subtitle` are used, as before.
- **The general flow is "Générale" in French.** Dutch stays "Algemeen". AXA needs no translation.
- **`App.vue` reads the name for the active language** on the picker card, the flow page heading and the header subtitle.
- **`scripts/check.mjs` fails a flow that translates its name in only some languages**, so one language cannot quietly fall back to another's word.

## Checked

- `npm run check`: 18 checks pass.
- `npm run build` passes.
- In a local preview with the language on French, the picker card, the flow page heading and the header subtitle read "Générale", and "Algemeen" no longer appears.

## Not checked

- The Dutch site was not looked at in a browser; its strings in `spec.json` are unchanged.
- No call was placed.

## After the merge

Netlify builds and publishes the site from `main`, as with #3.
params.title: Name the general flow in French on the French site
